claims.text: The starting CoCrFeNi alloy has a homogeneous microstructure.
The starting CoCrFeNi alloy contains no second-phase lubricants.
Adding a controlled volume fraction of h-BN to CoCrFeNi will produce a self-lubricating composite.
The proposed processing intervention can produce a uniform distribution of h-BN particulates in the CoCrFeNi matrix.
Evenly dispersed h-BN particles will form a continuous lubricative tribolayer under sliding.
At low temperatures, h-BN facilitates interfacial shear.
At low temperatures, h-BN accommodates contact stresses.
Interfacial shear and stress accommodation by h-BN reduce friction at low temperatures.
At high temperatures, h-BN remains sufficiently chemically stable to promote formation and maintenance of a protective lubricious film.
The h-BN-derived lubricious film mitigates adhesion-driven wear at high temperatures.
The h-BN-reinforced CoCrFeNi composite will maintain low friction from room temperature to 800 °C in an oxidizing environment.
The h-BN-reinforced composite will have a significantly lower coefficient of friction than unmodified CoCrFeNi across the entire room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
The h-BN-reinforced composite will have a reduced wear rate relative to unmodified CoCrFeNi across the entire room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
